_comment: What chat-sample.png contains, so the self-test can score itself.
The image is a real frame of a real game -- not a synthetic one -- and a
deliberately unkind one: 1919x1079, the chat box closed so the messages are
drawn faint straight over the game world, and 13px glyphs because the frame
came off a stream that had already downscaled the game. If the reading chain
handles this it handles a native client comfortably.
The chat is in English while the interface defaults to French, so the test
parses with the spell names below rather than with the user's own locale.
That is on purpose: the verdict then means 'the program works', not 'your
language setting is right', and it stays the same verdict on every install.
Champion names need no such table -- they resolve through the Data Dragon id,
which is the same in every language.
